hook.text: A student is described by five features: age, G P A, attendance, study hours and income. Five features, so d equals five.

why.text: Fewer features means less computation, cheaper data, and simpler models. With two, you can even plot the data.

why2.text: But fewer features does not promise higher accuracy. What matters is keeping the useful information.

sel.text: There are two ways to get fewer features. Feature selection keeps some of the original columns. Keep G P A and study hours, and drop the rest. They stay easy to read.

ext.text: Feature extraction builds new features out of the old ones. Height and weight become one new number: z one equals zero point six times height, plus zero point eight times weight.

fwd.text: How do you choose which columns to keep? Forward search starts with no features. It tries adding each one, and keeps the one with the lowest validation error.

fwd2.text: It goes on adding while the error improves. Backward search starts with all of them, and removes. Both are greedy, so neither guarantees the best subset.

pca.text: The best known extraction method is P C A: principal component analysis.

pca1.text: Here are students' heights and weights. First, centre the cloud, by subtracting the mean.

pca2.text: Now pick a direction, and project every point onto it. Some directions squeeze the points together. Others spread them out.

pca3.text: P C A picks the direction with the greatest spread: the largest variance. That is the first principal component.

pca4.text: The second is perpendicular to the first, and holds the next largest variance. Here the first keeps ninety two percent, and the second the other eight.

iris.text: On the iris data in the slides, two components keep ninety seven point seven seven percent of the variance.

trap.text: One trap. P C A never looks at the labels. The direction with the most spread is not always the one that separates the classes.

lda.text: When separating the classes is the goal, the slides name L D A, which uses the class labels.

ex3.text: Forward search adds. Backward search removes.

ex4.text: P C A keeps the direction of largest variance.

ex5.text: P C A ignores the labels.
